summary: Quarterly midyear update covering strategy tweaks, topline metrics, hiring posture, and org priorities. Leadership walked through product bets for Q3, hiring deceleration in low-priority buckets, stronger focus on Dedicated and Private go-to-market, and new reliability targets. People/HR covered benefits changes and interview timelines. Session ended with an open Q&A and clear next steps for managers.
topics: Product focus and roadmap adjustments (Marco / Elena)
transcript: [00:00] Maya Singh: alright thanks everyone for coming in on a Tuesday morning, gonna keep this tight, um — quick state of the company, high level, and then we'll go into product and hiring. if you have questions please put them in Q and A or drop them in slack #all-hands-questions.

[03:12] Marco Alvarez: quick slide, Q2 highlights — we hit 1.6x inference volume quarter over quarter, hosted revenue grew, and Dedicated pipeline is warming. note: when i say "Dedicated" i mean reserved capacity customers, the ones asking for SLAs and private peering.

[07:40] Maya Singh: major point — we are doubling down on serving economics. that means more tooling in Redwood Optimize — batch configs, KV cache improvements. we've seen cost per token drop 12% on workloads that use prefix caching. caveat: not every customer can change prompts, so we need better default configs.

[12:05] Sara Liu: engineering is focused on two things: reliability SLOs and latency P99. we had one incident last month around shard rebalancing that caused elevated tail latency for ~18 minutes, root cause was orchestration race when autoscaler spun up new pods, kafka to kinesis type of mismatch — sorry bad metaphor, um — scheduler state desync. fix is in canary now.

[16:30] Elena Rossi: on the runtime side we shipped kernel selector improvements for int8 quantized paths, that improves throughput on A100 and 80-gpu-ish machines — again imprecise phrasing — but engineers will put the deep notes in the tech blog. there were a few misreports in the community about our kv cache implementation; those are inaccurate, we still support prefix caching and KV eviction policies are pluggable.

[20:50] Priya Kapoor: hiring update — we are pausing a handful of non-critical roles and accelerating hiring for infra, reliability, and dedicated sales. headcount net is still positive but we are tightening prioritization. expected hiring cadence: two-week review cycles, managers must submit justification and impact metrics.

[25:00] Maya Singh: why the change? simple: units matter. as open models proliferate, customers choose where to run by economics. our bet is serving: low latency, predictable cost, and private deployments. so we move hiring budget toward teams that improve unit economics or accelerate Dedicated deals.

[29:43] James Kline: on the sales front, we've got three mid-market pilots for Dedicated that could convert in Q3. procurement timelines vary — some want SOC2 + attestation copies, others ask for VPC peering diagrams. ops note: ensure security package is in the customer portal by end of week.

[34:10] Employee (Engineering): question in chat — will we have more remote interviews or in-person loops? Priya: for senior ICs and critical infra roles we will do hybrid — panel loop via video and a short onsite for final bar raisers where feasible.

[38:00] Maya Singh: quick financial note — burn is within plan; revenue growth is good but still not profitable at company level; we are aiming to be cash-efficient while investing in product-market fit for Dedicated and Private. we won't go into numbers here, but finance doc will be shared.

[43:15] Marco Alvarez: product priorities for Q3: 1) improve streaming UX and function-calling reliability, 2) rollout autoscaling policies for Dedicated (burst to shared capacity), 3) UX polishing for model catalog and model pinning + rollouts. success metrics: lower latencies by 10% across the top 5 customers and increase Dedicated conversions by 25%.

[47:30] Sara Liu: note on incident ops — new on-call rota starts next week. we've reduced mean time to mitigate by adding automated rollback policies and fallback model variants; there will be a short training session — engineers please RSVP.

[51:05] Priya Kapoor: benefits Q: Yes, parental leave policy update is going through HR portal; also we are updating interview training — unconscious bias module will be required for all hiring managers before doing loops.

[55:20] Employee (Product): question — will we open source any of the runtime kernels? Elena: short answer: we plan to publish some components and benchmarks but core runtime optimizations and orchestration will remain proprietary; we'll share reproducible benchmarks and evaluator hooks.

[58:40] Maya Singh: wrap up — thank you. recap: managers submit hiring priorities, ops post security package, product to publish Q3 doc next week. um, one more — we'll have a smaller follow-up town hall focused on benefits during lunch next Thursday. thanks everyone, see you after the Q&A. (applause emoji in chat)
